topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
target_audience: University students with basic programming/linear algebra knowledge

sections.title: The Problem: Information Overload
lecture_lines: Like finding clues in a mystery.
animations: 1. Fade in text 'RNN' and 'Sequence'; show '...' between them.
2. Color '...' to red (#FF0000) to show the 'bottleneck' limitation.
3. Replace 'RNN' with a magnifying glass icon labeled 'Attention' (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: The Core Components: Query, Key, and Value
animations: 1. Display three boxes labeled Q, K, and V in colors #FF5733, #33FF57, #3357FF.
2. Show a magnifying glass (#FFFFFF) moving across the labels K (#33FF57), finding a match.
3. Move the corresponding V (#3357FF) into a final output vector (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Calculating Relevance: Dot Product & Softmax
animations: 1. Display a 3x3 grid showing a Dot Product matrix with numerical values (#FFFFFF).
2. Flash specific grid cells to highlight similarity using a heatmap (#FFFF00 to #FF0000).
3. Show the Softmax function mapping these values to a row summing to 1 (#00FF00).

sections.title: Bringing it Together: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
animations: 1. Display the Attention Weights (#FFFF00) and Value vectors (#3357FF).
2. Show visual lines connecting weights (#FFFF00) to values (#3357FF).
3. Transition to a single vector (#FFFFFF) representing the weighted sum.

sections.title: Application: Multi-Head Attention
animations: 1. Display three identical Attention modules (#FFFFFF) in parallel.
2. Highlight different connections in each module (e.g., green (#00FF00) for grammar, blue (#3357FF) for sentiment).
3. Concatenate the outputs into one final combined vector (#FFFFFF).
